summary: Small, correctly-scoped streaming parser fix: when an engine-based reasoning parser confirms the end of reasoning without emitting the following text as content (and it is paired with a text-based tool parser), the text after the end marker is recovered from the content token ids so the tool parser sees it. This fixes a regression where a batched `</think><tool_call>` delta dropped the leading `<`, causing the whole tool call to leak into content. The fix is well-guarded and comes with a genuine regression test.
actions_taken: Read the diff and confirmed changed files: vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py (5 added lines) and tests/parser/test_streaming.py (new test). `git diff --stat` confirms the diff adds only these; it touches no tool-call-id/kimi_k2 logic.

Read vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py around the reasoning->tool transition (parse_delta, lines ~793-925) plus __init__/_engine_based (lines 112-141), StreamState.advance/commit (44-83), and extract_content_ids delegation (212-224, 725-728) to understand the two distinct 'engine' notions: self._engine_based (both sub-parsers engine-based) vs reasoning_parser.engine_based_streaming. The fix is in the else branch (self._engine_based False), which is the mixed case: engine-based reasoning parser + text-based tool parser.

Traced the fix by hand for the batched `</think><` delta: reasoning end is confirmed via has_engine_confirmed_reasoning_end(); extract_content_ids(delta_token_ids) yields the trailing `<` token; delta_message is None so current_text is empty; the new `if not current_text and current_token_ids:` branch decodes the content ids back to `<`, which is then handed to the tool parser via previous_text on the next delta. Without it, the `<` is lost and Hermes2Pro never recognizes `<tool_call>`, leaking the call into content.

Verified the guard prevents double-emission/regression: when a text-based reasoning parser already returns trailing content as delta_message.content, current_text is truthy so the new branch is skipped; the decode only runs once per stream at the boundary, so no hot-path per-token cost.

Ran the new test: PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=... python -m pytest tests/parser/test_streaming.py::test_parse_delta_engine_reasoning_tool_batched_boundary -q -p no:cacheprovider -> 1 passed. It asserts the tool call is parsed (name get_weather, args {"city": "Dallas"}) and that 'tool_call' does not leak into content.

Ran the full file: pytest tests/parser/test_streaming.py -q -> 14 passed, 2 failed. The 2 failures (test_parse_delta_required_tool_choice_kimi_k2_ids and ..._after_history) are in kimi_k2 tool-call-id handling that this diff does not touch, so they pre-date this change and are not caused by it. Notably test_parse_delta_both_parsers (text-based reasoning + Hermes tool parser, asserting content == "") passes, confirming the fix does not regress the pure text-based reasoning path.
